messages.author: 3443c221829642df
messages.subject: shinyStan installation fails: problem with 'htmlwidgets'
parts:
Dear shinyStan-Team,

First off, great tool and I'd like to use it for a project I just started working on, in order to make my data and my analysis available on my website - great stuff! I tried installing shinyStan today, but got the following error message: 

ERROR: dependency 'htmlwidgets' is not available for package 'threejs'
* removing 'C:/Users/PViefers/Documents/R/win-library/3.1/threejs'
Error: Command failed (1)
In addition: Warning message:
package ‘htmlwidgets’ is not available (for R version 3.1.2) 

I am running R under Windows using Revolution R Open 8.0.1 beta

R version 3.1.2 (2014-10-31)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)

(...)

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base     

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] tools_3.1.2 

Thanks for your help,
Paul


PS: I hope this is the right place to ask, because it rejected the tag 'shinyStan'.

I've added a tag for 'shinyStan' on the stan-users list, so you should be able to use that tag in the future.

Thanks for helping diagnose installation problems.


Daniel

messages.subject: Re: shinyStan installation fails: problem with 'htmlwidgets'
parts:
Jonah,
Absolutely no need to apologize, it's a great tool and I am happy to test it and in case report minor problems... really, it wasn't shinyStan's fault here.

Now for the mirror, I unfortunately changed it before checking which one I was using, but if I had to guess it was Berlin (softliste.de) because that used to be closest to my location. I now use University of Münster's and that worked. 

To check that I removed htmlwidgets again and cycled through all mirrors in Germany (there only four) to replicate the error- nothing. They all work, maybe I changed the mirror while I was abroad and had to install a package, but then I really don't know a way how to trace which mirror it was. Can you infer that somehow from the installed packages maybe?

Best,
Paul
